question: Under what geometric conditions can an unknown low-dimensional signal model be identified from incomplete linear measurements alone, using either several sensing operators or a single operator plus known group invariance?

key_findings.claim: Measurement consistency under one rank-deficient operator cannot by itself identify a reconstruction or signal model because arbitrary nullspace-valued corrections remain invisible.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 1 writes every consistent reconstruction as A-dagger y plus an arbitrary function valued in null(A). The characteristic-function argument likewise shows that finitely many projections of a full-dimensional distribution reveal only a finite union of proper subspaces, so low dimensionality or other structure is essential rather than a convenience.

key_findings.claim: With G independent m-by-n operators, full stacked rank is necessary and, for a k-dimensional compact or conic signal set, generic model identification is sufficient when m exceeds k+n/G.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 3 requires the vertical stack of all operators to have rank n, hence m at least n/G for equal-sized operators. Theorem 4 proves that almost every operator tuple identifies the support from its projected sets when m>k+n/G; with many operators, model identification may therefore need fewer measurements per individual sample than unique signal recovery.

key_findings.claim: Group invariance converts one physical operator into related virtual operators, but identifiability depends on irreducible-representation multiplicities rather than simply the number of group elements.
key_findings.evidence: For an invariant support, y=Ax can be reinterpreted as y=AT_g x-prime for another valid signal. Proposition 8 gives the necessary bound m at least max_j c_j/s_j. For compact cyclic groups, Theorem 9 proves generic sufficiency at m>2k+max_j c_j+1, equivalent to max_j c_j/s_j because cyclic irreducibles are one-dimensional; the analogous statement for arbitrary compact groups is explicitly only Conjecture 10.

anchors.section: 4 Learning with a Single Operator and Group Symmetry

key_findings.claim: An equivariant forward operator defeats the invariance strategy because all virtual operators share the same nullspace.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 11 proves equivalence between shared nullspaces for {AT_g} and the existence of an output representation satisfying AT_g=T-tilde_g A. Consequently, shift invariance cannot fill missing frequencies for partial-Fourier operators such as deblurring, super-resolution, or fixed-mask MRI, whereas a non-equivariant mask or a compatible different symmetry can expose new directions.

key_findings.claim: The theorems establish noiseless population identifiability, not finite-sample learnability, stable inversion, or algorithmic convergence; the noise extension preserves uniqueness only under strong deconvolution assumptions.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 12 says a known independent noise law with nowhere-zero characteristic function uniquely maps noisy to clean measurement distributions. The paper repeatedly states that this makes no sample-complexity claim, and its conclusion leaves robustness to noise open. Synthetic subspace and MNIST experiments show threshold-like behavior, but finite networks need margins beyond theoretical boundaries and structured masks deviate from generic-operator predictions.

method.core_idea: View each observed measurement set as a geometric projection of an unknown low-dimensional support, intersect the lifted projection-consistent sets, and characterize when generic independent or group-related operators leave no aliases.
method.mechanism: For independent sensing, stacked-rank and box-counting arguments bound the dimension of false supports consistent with every projected set. For a single operator, signal-set invariance supplies virtual operators AT_g; representation theory decomposes the action into irreducible blocks and identifies the largest multiplicity-to-dimension ratio as the nullspace-coverage bottleneck. A separate equivariance theorem characterizes sensing maps that provide no new virtual nullspaces.
assumptions: The forward maps are known linear operators and the main identification analysis is at the level of exact population measurement sets or distributions.
The signal support is compact with upper box-counting dimension k, or is a conic set whose intersection with the unit sphere has dimension k-1.
Sufficient conditions hold for almost every operator in Lebesgue measure and need not hold for structured sensing families.
For the proved single-operator sufficiency theorem, the acting group is compact and cyclic and its action is an exact invertible linear representation.
Signal recovery and distribution identification require additional injectivity/measurability conditions beyond support identification.
The noise proposition assumes independent additive noise with a known distribution and a characteristic function that is nowhere zero.
Continuous transformations are reduced to a finite-dimensional exact action through bandlimited signals and ideal anti-aliasing.

techniques.role: Lifts each measured support through its operator nullspace and intersects the lifted sets to define all model aliases.
Controls the generic linear maps that remain injective on low-dimensional difference or alias sets.
Provides the basic necessary coverage condition for several independent sensing operators.
Reinterprets one invariant signal population as observations under the family AT_g without paired transformed samples.
Quantifies how much of the ambient space a group orbit can expose to one sensing map.
Detects sensing designs for which symmetry creates no additional nullspace information.
Transfers population identifiability from clean to known additive-noise measurement laws.

evaluations.setting: Gaussian k-dimensional subspaces in ambient dimension 50 observed through several independent Gaussian operators.
evaluations.metric: Probability over 25 trials that nuclear-norm matrix completion reconstructs the sample matrix to relative error below 0.1.
evaluations.result: For k equal to 1, 10, and 40, the empirical transition follows the generic m>k+n/G boundary.
evaluations.baseline: Sensing configurations below the theorem's sufficient boundary.

evaluations.setting: The same subspace recovery experiment with group-related shifted or reflected operators.
evaluations.metric: Probability of successful matrix completion across m and group choice.
evaluations.result: Typical transitions occur near m approximately k+max c_j/s_j, about k below the cyclic theorem's worst-case sufficient bound; the authors attribute the additional k to adversarial models such as their reflection counterexample.
evaluations.baseline: Theorem 9's worst-case boundary and its necessary multiplicity boundary.

evaluations.setting: MNIST reconstructed by a fully connected bottleneck autoencoder from samples split across up to 40 Gaussian sensing operators.
evaluations.metric: Test PSNR and qualitative reconstruction across measurements and operator counts.
evaluations.result: The non-residual bottleneck reaches 21.36 dB for G=40 and m=100 versus 10.02 dB for the pseudoinverse; a residual architecture that can copy its input reaches only 10.32 dB. The phase diagram broadly follows m>k+n/G.
evaluations.baseline: Pseudoinverse and a residual autoencoder capable of the trivial measurement-consistent identity solution.

evaluations.setting: MNIST with multiple random inpainting masks rather than generic Gaussian operators.
evaluations.metric: Test PSNR over numbers of masks and observed pixels.
evaluations.result: The generic theorem remains a rough lower boundary, but additional measurements are needed, plausibly because sparse masks are coherent with sparse digit images and occupy a measure-zero operator family.

evaluations.setting: Shift-invariant and rotation/reflection-invariant augmented MNIST learned from one Gaussian operator using equivariant imaging.
evaluations.metric: Test PSNR versus compression ratio, compared with supervised, plain unsupervised, and pseudoinverse reconstruction.
evaluations.result: Plain measurement consistency collapses to pseudoinverse quality. Equivariant training approaches supervised performance only above a finite margin: roughly m/n>0.07 for shifts and m/n at least 0.2 for rotations/reflections, consistent qualitatively with representation multiplicities but not a sharp finite-sample theorem.
evaluations.baseline: Supervised U-Net, unsupervised U-Net without equivariance, and the linear pseudoinverse.

limitations: Author-stated: the results are geometric population-identifiability bounds and do not quantify the number of training samples needed.
Author-stated: stability to measurement perturbations and robust sample complexity are outside scope; the additive-noise result is uniqueness by exact distribution deconvolution.
Author-stated: the sufficient single-operator theorem is proved only for compact cyclic groups, while the general compact-group form is conjectural.
Author-stated: approximately low-dimensional, compressible, heavy-tailed, and scale-semigroup models require extensions.
Reviewer inference: almost-everywhere guarantees may poorly predict highly structured operators such as masks, Fourier trajectories, Radon sampling, or hardware-constrained designs.
Reviewer inference: exact group invariance, ideal bandlimiting, and exact equivariance are strong approximations for natural images on discrete grids.
Reviewer inference: support identifiability does not imply stable per-sample recovery, correct density estimation, optimization success, or immunity to neural architectural shortcuts.
Reviewer inference: model dimension k is treated as known and fixed, yet estimating it reliably from incomplete noisy observations is itself nontrivial.
failure_modes: A single incomplete operator with no valid invariance leaves arbitrary nullspace aliases.
An equivariant sensing operator shares its nullspace across all symmetry-generated virtual operators, nullifying the invariance benefit.
A structured operator can lie in the exceptional measure-zero set even when its dimensions satisfy the generic sufficient inequality.
Approximate rather than exact data invariance can make an equivariance loss enforce a biased support.
Finite samples may not populate each projected support densely enough to identify the model despite population uniqueness.
Noise laws with zeros or near-zeros in their characteristic function make distribution deconvolution non-unique or severely ill-conditioned.
An expressive reconstruction network can minimize measurement consistency through an identity/pseudoinverse shortcut instead of learning a low-dimensional range.
The cyclic worst-case bound may be overly conservative for typical models, while applying it to a small subgroup of a non-cyclic action may discard useful symmetries.
reusable_insights: Audit whether augmentations actually rotate the sensing nullspace; data symmetry alone is insufficient.
Distinguish model-support identification, density identification, per-instance recovery, and stable recovery because their measurement thresholds differ.
Count independent measurement directions supplied by symmetry through representation multiplicities rather than raw group size.
Use operator diversity as a dataset-design variable: different samples need not be repeated measurements of the same latent signal.
Block trivial measurement-consistent shortcuts with an explicit low-dimensional bottleneck or other independently justified model constraint.
Treat an almost-everywhere identifiability boundary as a sensing-design screen, then test the actual structured operator numerically and spectrally.
Report finite-sample margins above population thresholds rather than presenting identifiability as a performance guarantee.
open_questions: Can Conjecture 10 be proved for arbitrary compact non-abelian groups with a tight dependence on c_j/s_j?
What are minimax sample-complexity and stability rates under finite noisy observations for broad k-dimensional supports?
How should the bounds change under approximate invariance, approximate low dimensionality, or unknown intrinsic dimension?
Can sensing operators be optimized under hardware constraints to maximize virtual-nullspace coverage while retaining reconstruction stability?
What replaces the group argument for useful noninvertible semigroups such as scale transformations?
Can algorithm-specific guarantees rule out neural shortcut solutions and prove convergence to the identifiable support?
How ill-conditioned is the characteristic-function deconvolution in realistic noise regimes even when uniqueness formally holds?
Can current diffusion objectives achieve the geometric boundary without requiring stronger corruption diversity assumptions?

competitive_landscape.title: AmbientGAN: Generative models from lossy measurements
competitive_landscape.difference: AmbientGAN trains an implicit distribution by passing generated samples through the known measurement process and states recoverability for identifiable corruption models. The reviewed paper supplies explicit geometric thresholds for general low-dimensional supports and finite operator families, independent of GAN parameterization or adversarial optimization.

competitive_landscape.title: Equivariant Imaging: Learning Beyond the Range Space
competitive_landscape.difference: Equivariant Imaging introduces the single-operator training loss and demonstrates CT and inpainting performance. The reviewed paper explains when that mechanism can identify a model, derives representation-dependent bounds, and identifies equivariant forward operators as a fundamental failure case.

competitive_landscape.title: Unsupervised Learning From Incomplete Measurements for Inverse Problems
competitive_landscape.difference: This same-team NeurIPS work develops the practical multi-operator loss, experiments on MRI/compressed sensing/inpainting, and contains the independent-operator bound. The reviewed paper subsumes that geometry and adds the substantially new single-operator group-representation theory and equivariant-sensor obstruction.

competitive_landscape.title: Robust Equivariant Imaging: A Fully Unsupervised Framework for Learning To Image From Noisy and Partial Measurements
competitive_landscape.difference: REI combines equivariant imaging with SURE and empirically handles noisy linear and nonlinear inverse problems. The sensing-theorem paper proves only population uniqueness under a known deconvolvable additive noise law and explicitly leaves robust finite-sample behavior open.

competitive_landscape.title: Ambient Diffusion: Learning Clean Distributions from Corrupted Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Ambient Diffusion adds a second corruption during denoising and proves conditional-expectation recovery under corruption-specific conditions, scaling to images with 90% missing pixels and MRI fine-tuning. It gives a concrete high-capacity learner, whereas the reviewed work gives model-class-agnostic identifiability thresholds but no diffusion objective or sample rate.

competitive_landscape.title: Equivariant Splitting: Self-Supervised Learning from Incomplete Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Equivariant Splitting combines virtual group-related operators with measurement splitting and equivariant architectures to obtain an unbiased supervised-risk estimate and MMSE optimality under rank conditions. This strengthens the algorithmic objective beyond the reviewed paper's identifiability result, while relying on comparable invariance and operator-coverage structure.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims necessary and generic sufficient sensing conditions for identifying arbitrary low-dimensional signal models from incomplete measurements, including the first representation-theoretic treatment of a single operator with group-invariant data.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Stacked-rank necessity, box-dimension sufficiency for independent operators, multiplicity bounds and a cyclic-group theorem, the equivariant-forward-map characterization, and controlled subspace/MNIST phase diagrams support a broad algorithm-agnostic theory.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The separation of model identification from signal recovery and the c_j/s_j symmetry bottleneck are substantive conceptual advances over AmbientGAN and Equivariant Imaging. The reach is narrower than the headline may suggest: general compact groups remain conjectural, population uniqueness omits sample/stability/optimization complexity, and newer ambient-diffusion and equivariant-splitting work provides stronger algorithm-specific objectives under additional assumptions.

reviewer_notes: Read all 41 extracted pages, including definitions of support and distribution identifiability, independent-operator geometry and proof, compact-group representation preliminaries, cyclic sufficiency and reflection counterexample, the equivariant-operator theorem, noise deconvolution, generative and reconstruction objectives, all subspace/MNIST experiments, and appendices proving the dimension and representation claims. Six primary OpenReview/arXiv/CVF/NeurIPS records covering ambient GANs, both direct precursor frameworks, robust noise handling, ambient diffusion, and the 2026 equivariant-splitting successor were checked on 2026-08-23.
